 Jake Dickert agrees to new Wake Forest contract, rebuffing coaching carousel interest
 The new long-term deal boosts staff and roster salary pools while shutting down outside interest from open jobs like Florida State as the No. 13 Demon Deacons push for an ACC title
 By
 Shehan Jeyarajah 
 Nov 12, 2026
 at
 5:41 pm ET 
 •
 3 min read
 Getty Images 
 Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert has agreed to a new contract that will significantly increase his staff and roster salary pools. The new contract keeps Dickert in Winston-Salem long term and rebuffs interest from the biggest jobs on the market. 
 Dickert has done a sensational job at Wake Forest, recording a 17-5 record, including 8-1 this season with the only loss coming against Miami . His 9-4 debut campaign marked the most wins ever by a first-year coach at Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons rank No. 13 in the most recent College Football Playoff Rankings. 
 "Wake Forest University is committed to football success at the highest level and Coach Dickert has done an extraordinary job of inspiring belief among our players, fans and the entire Demon Deacon community," Wake Forest athletic director John Currie said in a statement. "I am grateful for his and Candice's commitment and trust and especially appreciate President Rodriguez and our Board leadership recognizing that now was the time to go ahead and eliminate any outside speculation so that our team and Deacon Nation can put all our energy into the stretch run of this special season."
 With Dickert secured, eyes will soon turn to offensive coordinator Rob Ezell and quarterback Gio Lopez . Ezell is in his first year as a playcaller at the Power Four level and is leading the No. 9 offense in the sport. Lopez has an 18-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio and the No. 8 QBR nationally. 
 No. 13 Wake Forest travels to face SMU on Saturday, with the winner taking over the new favorite to reach the ACC Championship Game against Miami. 
 Candice and I have such a high level of appreciation for everyone involved at Wake Forest that believes in us and the future of our football program. We know what the path ahead looks like and we are excited to be a huge part of the future. As always, we need ALL of Demon… https://t.co/5TlEYX5MmS 
— Jake Dickert (@CoachDickert) November 12, 2026 
 Meteoric rise
 Dickert's rise from a wide receiver at Wisconsin-Stevens Point to a sought-after ACC coach is truly unique. Two years after graduating, he was on staff at North Dakota State as safeties coach and subsequently worked his way up from Division II Augustana and Minnesota State to the FBS. 
 In 2021, he was elevated to interim coach following Nick Rolovich's abrupt dismissal and quickly shepherded Washington State to consistency. Despite dealing with the mess of the collapsing Pac-12, Dickert went 23-20 with the Cougars and helped them reach the Holiday Bowl. 
 Now, he's been a sensational stabilizer at Wake Forest, taking them to the next level in the NIL era. Former coach Dave Clawson found consistent success as a developmental coach, and Dickert has taken his culture into 2026. 
 Lopez's sensational run
 Wake Forest quarterback Gio Lopez was a reclamation project after a mediocre season at North Carolina, thrust into a messy situation with Bill Belichick. Since reuniting with Ezell, an assistant during his successful run at South Alabama, Lopez has hit another level. 
 The junior is completing 67% of his passes for 2,176 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. He also ran for 317 yards and six touchdowns. He ranks top-three in the ACC in nearly every passing category, along with SMU's Kevin Jennings and Miami's Darian Mensah. 
 With Dickert locked in, Wake Forest's top priority should be enticing both Ezell and Lopez to stick around. If they do, it will make the Demon Deacons one of the most interesting teams of the offseason. 
 Resetting the coach market
 Dickert was repeatedly mentioned as a hot name in the coaching carousel after his impressive job at Wake Forest. He was elevated to head coach at Washington State in 2021, ultimately leading the Cougars to an 8-4 record and three bowl games in four years. 
 Because of his newfound ties to the ACC, Dickert was a popular name at Florida State to help solidify the program. With Dickert now off the board, Florida State's search now turns elsewhere, including towards former coach Jimbo Fisher. Duke's Manny Diaz and Arizona State's Kenny Dillingham have also been rumored for the move.
